records.label: Kindred I

phenotypes.text: elevated plasma renin activity decreasing to near normal

quotes: In kindred I, the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) and responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day).
In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr; however, the PRA decreased gradually to near normal values.
The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.

records.label: Four dominant and one sporadic PHA1 kindreds with MLR mutations
records.segregation: Mutations segregated with PHA1 and were not found in unaffected subjects
quotes: have identified heterozygous mutations in one sporadic and four dominant kindreds. These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
These mutations segregate with PHA1 and are not found in unaffected subjects.

records.label: Japanese family with renal PHA1

phenotypes.text: renal form of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 (mineralocorticoid resistance)

records.segregation: heterozygous mutation found in all affected members
quotes: We studied the molecular mechanisms of one Japanese family with a renal form of PHA1.
PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.

records.label: Sporadic case
records.segregation: Asymptomatic family members did not carry the mutation
quotes: In the sporadic case we identified a new frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the hMR gene. Family members were asymptomatic and had no mutation.
This mutation is the first described in exon 9 and impairs the last 27 amino acids of the hormone-binding domain.

records.label: 2 autosomal dominant PHA1 kindreds
quotes: We here report the results of a genetic study in a sporadic case and in 5 affected patients from 2 families with autosomal dominant PHA1.
In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 we found no mutation of the hMR gene.

records.label: 14 families with autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1
quotes: We have analyzed the human mineralocorticoid receptor (hMR) gene in 14 families with autosomal dominant or sporadic pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA1), a rare form of mineralocorticoid resistance characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting and failure to thrive. Six heterozygous mutations were detected.

Two frameshift mutations in exon 2 (insT1354, del8bp537) and one nonsense mutation in exon 4 (C2157A, Cys645stop) generate truncated proteins due to premature stop codons. Three missense mutations (G633R, Q776R, L979P) differently affect hMR function.

records.label: Patient with c.1131dupT
quotes: Six heterozygous NR3C2 mutations were detected. One frameshift mutation (c.1131dupT) has been reported previously.

records.label: Patient with c.2871dupC
quotes: The second frameshift mutation (c.2871dupC), which has only recently been reported by our group, showed no aldosterone binding and no transactivation because of a major change in receptor conformation.

records.label: Patients with novel nonsense mutations
quotes: Two novel nonsense mutations generate a truncated receptor protein.

records.label: Patient with S818L
quotes: S818L was reported recently without complete in vitro data. S818L does not bind aldosterone or activate transcription or translocate into the nucleus.

records.label: Patient with E972G
quotes: The novel E972G mutation showed a significantly lower ligand-binding affinity and only 9% of wild-type transcriptional activity caused by major changes in receptor conformation.

records.label: 33 PHA1 patients with MR gene abnormalities
quotes: A total of 22 MR gene abnormalities were found in 33 patients.

notes.statement: Pujo et al. (2007) performed a comprehensive screen of the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MR; NR3C2) in PHA1 patients, looking for nucleotide substitutions in coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons, as well as for large deletions. They found 22 MR gene abnormalities in 33 patients. They concluded that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified by aldosterone and potassium levels.
quotes: We present the first comprehensive study seeking nucleotide substitutions in coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons, as well as for large deletions.
A total of 22 MR gene abnormalities were found in 33 patients.
We demonstrate that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels

notes.statement: Pujo et al. (2007) found that a genocopy might exist in 3 PHA1 kindreds without MR mutations. They suggested that the other patients without MR mutations might have different disorders that resemble PHA1 in the neonatal period.
quotes: In our study the possibility of a genocopy exists in three PHA1 kindreds.
The other patients without MR mutations might have different diseases resembling to PHA1 in the neonatal period, which could be identified by extensive clinical and functional exploration.

notes.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) identified 6 heterozygous NR3C2 mutations in 6 patients with PHA1: 2 frameshift mutations (c.1131dupT and c.2871dupC), 2 novel nonsense mutations predicted to generate a truncated receptor, and 2 missense mutations (S818L and E972G).
quotes: Six heterozygous NR3C2 mutations were detected.
Two novel nonsense mutations generate a truncated receptor protein. Two missense mutations differently affect MR function.

notes.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) found that the c.2871dupC frameshift mutant showed no aldosterone binding and no transactivation due to a major change in receptor conformation, and that the S818L mutant did not bind aldosterone, activate transcription, or translocate into the nucleus, with 3-dimensional modeling showing major displacement of several residues involved in aldosterone binding.
quotes: showed no aldosterone binding and no transactivation because of a major change in receptor conformation
S818L does not bind aldosterone or activate transcription or translocate into the nucleus. A major displacement of several residues involved in aldosterone binding was PHA1 causing.

notes.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) found that the E972G mutant mineralocorticoid receptor had significantly lower ligand-binding affinity and only 9% of wildtype transcriptional activity, attributed to major changes in receptor conformation.
quotes: The novel E972G mutation showed a significantly lower ligand-binding affinity and only 9% of wild-type transcriptional activity caused by major changes in receptor conformation.

notes.statement: RAINE and ROY (1962) described a salt-losing syndrome in infancy, which they called pseudo-hypoadrenocorticalism.
quotes: A salt-losing syndrome in infancy. Pseudo-hypoadrenocorticalism.

notes.statement: DONNELL et al. (1959) described pseudohypoadrenalocorticism, a disorder of renal sodium loss, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia that they attributed to renal tubular insensitivity to mineralocorticoids.
quotes: Pseudohypo-adrenalocorticism; renal sodium loss, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia due to a renal tubular insensitivity to mineralocorticoids.

notes.statement: CHEEK and PERRY (1958) described a salt-wasting syndrome in infancy.
quotes: A salt wasting syndrome in infancy.

notes.statement: Sartorato et al. (2003) found that the DNA-binding domain mutant G633R showed reduced maximal transactivation with normal binding characteristics and ED50, whereas ligand-binding domain mutants Q776R and L979P showed reduced or absent aldosterone binding, respectively, with reduced or absent ligand-dependent transactivation.
quotes: The DNA binding domain mutant R633 exhibits reduced maximal transactivation, although its binding characteristics and ED(50) of transactivation are comparable with wild-type hMR.
Ligand binding domain mutants R776 and P979 present reduced or absent aldosterone binding, respectively, which is associated with reduced or absent ligand-dependent transactivation capacity.

notes.statement: Sartorato et al. (2003) found that the L979P mutant had a transdominant negative effect on wildtype MR activity, whereas G633R and Q776R probably resulted in haploinsufficiency.
quotes: Finally, P979 possesses a transdominant negative effect on wild-type hMR activity, whereas mutations G633R and Q776R probably result in haploinsufficiency in PHA1 patients.

notes.statement: Sartorato et al. (2003) found MR mutations in 70% of their familial cases of autosomal dominant PHA1; the absence of mutations in some families suggested that other genes may be involved.
quotes: We conclude that hMR mutations are a common feature of autosomal dominant PHA1, being found in 70% of our familial cases. Their absence in some families underscores the importance of an extensive investigation of the hMR gene and the role of precise diagnostic procedures to allow for identification of other genes potentially involved in the disease.

notes.statement: Viemann et al. (2001) found no mutation in the hMR gene in 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 and concluded that autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a genetically heterogeneous disease involving other, as yet unidentified, genes.
quotes: In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 we found no mutation of the hMR gene.
Our results confirm the hypothesis that autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a genetically heterogeneous disease involving other, as yet unidentified, genes.

notes.statement: Viemann et al. (2001) noted that PHA1 is characterized by neonatal salt wasting resistant to mineralocorticoids, and that the autosomal dominant or sporadic form shows milder symptoms that remit with age, in contrast to the autosomal recessive form caused by mutations in the amiloride-sensitive sodium channel.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 (PHA1) is characterized by neonatal salt wasting resistant to mineralocorticoids.
the autosomal dominant or sporadic form, which shows milder symptoms that remit with age.

notes.statement: Tajima et al. (2000) found that, in transfected COS-1 cells with a GRE-tk-CAT reporter, aldosterone increased CAT activity with wildtype mineralocorticoid receptor but had no effect with the L924P mutant receptor. They suggested that mineralocorticoid resistance in the family was caused by this missense mutation, the first missense MR mutation reported in renal PHA1.
quotes: Aldosterone increased CAT activity in cells expressing wild-type receptor, but had no effect in cells expressing the mutant receptors.
To our knowledge, this is the first case of the missense mutation of the MR gene in renal PHA1.

notes.statement: Geller et al. (1998) described PHA1 as neonatal renal salt wasting with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis even though aldosterone levels are elevated. They stated that the autosomal dominant or sporadic form is milder than the recessive form and remits with age.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1) is characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis, despite elevated aldosterone levels.
Autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a milder disease that remits with age.

notes.statement: Geller et al. (1998) found no ENaC gene mutations in 6 dominant and 7 sporadic PHA1 kindreds, which pointed to mutations in other genes. MLR mutations were found in only 5 of these 13 kindreds.
quotes: Among six dominant and seven sporadic PHA1 kindreds, we have found no ENaC gene mutations, implicating mutations in other genes.

notes.statement: Geller et al. (1998) concluded that heterozygous MLR mutations cause PHA1. They stated that this underscores the role of mineralocorticoid receptor function in regulating salt and blood pressure homeostasis in humans.
quotes: These findings demonstrate that heterozygous MLR mutations cause PHA1, underscore the important role of mineralocorticoid receptor function in regulation of salt and blood pressure homeostasis in humans

notes.statement: Armanini et al. (1985) found high-affinity [3H]aldosterone binding (Kd about 3 nM; 150 to 600 sites per cell) in control monocytes. Binding was absent in 2 patients with pseudohypoaldosteronism and reduced in a third. The authors concluded that the disorder appeared to be caused by a type I (mineralocorticoid) receptor defect that may be complete or partial.
quotes: Percoll-separated control monocytes bound [3H]aldosterone with high affinity (Kd approximately 3 nM) and limited capacity (150 to 600 sites per cell).
It appears that pseudohypoaldosteronism is caused by a Type I receptor defect, that the defect may be complete or partial

notes.statement: Armanini et al. (1985) suggested that transmission of pseudohypoaldosteronism may be autosomal recessive. They based this on an affected sib pair whose parents were first cousins and had normal monocyte aldosterone receptor levels.
quotes: Levels in the parents of the Munich patients (first cousins) were normal.
that transmission may be autosomal recessive

notes.statement: Armanini et al. (1985) described pseudohypoaldosteronism as a salt-wasting syndrome with failure to thrive that usually presents in infancy. Features include high urinary sodium despite hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism, a syndrome characterized by salt wasting and failure to thrive, usually presents in infancy as high urinary levels of sodium despite hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels.

notes.statement: Hanukoglu (1991) found that in a kindred with renal PHA I, clinical expression in 7 additional members across 3 generations ranged from asymptomatic to moderate. The propositus no longer needed sodium supplementation after age 2 years. Hyperaldosteronism persisted for 13 years while PRA fell, which the author took to indicate tertiary hyperaldosteronism from an autonomously functioning zona glomerulosa.
quotes: Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two. In seven additional family members from three generations, clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate.
Persistent hyperaldosteronism in the face of a decrease in PRA indicated the development of tertiary hyperaldosteronism due to autonomously functioning zona glomerulosa.

notes.statement: Hanukoglu (1991) concluded that type I PHA includes 2 clinically and genetically distinct entities. One is a renal form with autosomal dominant transmission. The other is a multiple target organ form with autosomal recessive inheritance, seen in a girl from a consanguineous family who had severe salt wasting and increased salivary and sweat electrolytes.
quotes: She had also increased salivary and sweat electrolytes consistent with PHA resulting from multiple organ unresponsiveness to mineralocorticoids.
This pedigree was consistent with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.
we conclude that type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects.
